title: Finite normalization at persistent nodes over an arbitrary trait
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring with fraction field $K$, residue field $k$, and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $X\to S$ be projective [def-kun-projective], flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with nonempty nodal geometric fibres. Let $N_K$ be the reduced singular subscheme of $X_K$, and let $N\subset X$ be its scheme-theoretic closure. Then $N$ is finite etale over $S$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. The normalization $\nu:C\to X$, defined on reduced affine rings by integral closure in the product of their component fraction fields, is finite. The family $C\to S$ is projective, flat and finitely presented, with nodal geometric fibres and smooth generic fibre [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. The map $\nu$ is an isomorphism over $X\setminus N$. The inverse image $B=C\times_XN$ lies in the relative smooth locus of $C$, is finite etale over $S$, and $B\to N$ is finite etale of constant degree two. The square with vertices $B,C,N,X$ is a pushout of schemes [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. For every open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ [def-weil-open-immersion], the square of the inverse images of $V$ in $B$, $C$, $N$ and $V$ itself is again a pushout of schemes. The coordinate rings of $N$ and $B$ are the integral closures of $R$ in their generic finite algebras; these schemes and their map are therefore determined by their generic finite schemes. The generic square is the normalization and conductor square of $X_K$. The empty case is allowed. A nodal geometric fibre here is reduced of pure dimension one, and each nonsmooth closed point has completed local ring $\Omega[[x,y]]/(xy)$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. The intermediate geometric fibres need not be connected. The map $B\to C$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Here $X$ is reduced, and scheme-theoretic closure is the scheme-theoretic image of the generic immersion [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. The finite etale schemes $N$ and $B$ are regular semilocal schemes of dimension one when nonempty; their local rings at closed points are DVRs in which a uniformizer of $R$ is a uniformizer.

proof.text: Apply the normalization-atlas lemma to $X/S$. It gives reducedness of $X$, the finite surjective normalization $C\to X$, all asserted family properties of $C/S$, and the canonical generic normalization. The affine-normalization lemma identifies this with integral closure in component fraction fields on every reduced affine open.

source.place: Tag 0CDD; extracted normalization atlas and affine calculation

proof.text: The singular-closure-atlas lemma applies to that same atlas: it gives $N$ and $B$ finite etale over $S$, $B\to N$ finite etale of degree two, the closed immersion into the smooth locus, the isomorphism away from $N$, and the generic conductor ideal. Its chart identification $N_K=N\times_SK$ identifies the generic square with the normalization and conductor square.

source.place: Tag 0CDD; extracted horizontal-closure and conductor atlas

proof.text: On each persistent model $Q=R'[u,v]/(uv)$ (or $K'[u,v]/(uv)$ on a generic split chart) the split-node algebra lemma gives $Q\cong E\times_{R'\times R'}R'$ with $E\to R'\times R'$ surjective, i.e. the exact difference sequence $0\to Q\to E\oplus R'\to R'\times R'\to0$; and $\operatorname{Spec}E\to\operatorname{Spec}Q$ is finite and $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}Q$ a closed immersion. By the normalization atlas and the closure atlas, on the common chart $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}P_a\to\operatorname{Spec}Q$ (etale, so $P_a$ is flat over $Q$) the inverse images of $C,N,B$ are $\operatorname{Spec}$ of $P_a\otimes_QE$, $P_a\otimes_QR'$, $P_a\otimes_Q(R'\times R')$. The pinching-descent lemma applied to $\operatorname{Spec}Q$ with its identity chart, and its flat-algebra clause with $H=P_a$, shows that the sequence stays exact on $U_a$. On every other chart the square is the identity with $B=N=\varnothing$. Applied to $X$ with this atlas, its criterion proves the scheme pushout and every open-restriction pushout.

source.place: Tags 0ET0 and 0BMP; extracted affine pinching descent

proof.text: Apply finite-etale generic components to $N/S$ and $B/S$, since the DVR is normal integral Noetherian. Their coordinate rings are the integral closures in the respective generic finite algebras. A generic algebra map preserves monic equations, hence integral elements; it restricts uniquely to those subrings. Thus both schemes and their map are determined by their generic data.

For either finite etale $R$-algebra $T$, all maximal ideals lie over $(\pi)$ and correspond to maximal ideals of the finite-dimensional algebra $T/\pi T$, so $T$ is semilocal. Its component decomposition gives domain local rings. At a closed point $t$, $T_t/\pi T_t$ is a field, so its maximal ideal is $(\pi)$; flatness makes $\pi$ nonzero and a nonzerodivisor. Noetherianity and the DVR characterization give a DVR with that uniformizer and dimension one. Generic local rings are fields, proving regularity and dimension one when nonempty. If $N_K=\varnothing$, the atlas gives $N=B=\varnothing$, $C=X$; the empty-base degree-two and pushout assertions still hold.
